# `shell/Desktop.js`

## Classes

### `class Desktop`

Desktop.js — the OS shell compositor. Owns: - Plauna workspace (virtual desktops, panel chrome, window management). - Taskbar (bottom bar: start menu + running apps + status tray). - NotificationCenter (toast/banner delivery). - Routing of kernel 'ui:open-panel' events to WorkspaceManager. Phase 2 adds AppManifestLoader → dynamic app registration. Phase 3 adds GPU panel wiring (canvas surface allocation per app).

## Functions

### `createEchoAvatarPresentationCapability(client)`

Give selected built-in editors presentation access to the stable Echo actor. The facade deliberately omits the runtime port, host lifecycle, visibility, boot-completion, shell binding, and every command/tool capability. Validation remains inside RuntimeEchoAvatarClient at the stable-host boundary.

### `createNaviEchoEvolutionPresentationCapability(gateway)`

Give AI Echo a closed view of verified appearance lineage, the kernel's lock-preserving candidate transform, and the one append-only operator appearance commit. The only developmental input is a closed correction or praise signal; raw conversation content and generic evidence stay absent.

### `createNaviDevelopmentPresentationCapability(gateway)`

Only the trusted AI Echo review surface receives developmental mutations.

### `createNaviVoicePresentationCapability(gateway)`

Data and user-operated controls only; provider registration stays in the kernel.

### `createProvisionalMountHandoff({ controller = new AbortController()`

Own teardown while an async app mount is still provisional. Cancellation calls an attached cleanup synchronously, so the app observes its AbortSignal before the panel is removed. The unmount facade returns that cleanup promise so a committed panel close can finish the app before closing its sandbox. Cancellation before cleanup is attached remains non-blocking; attach() starts the cleanup as soon as the provisional mount resolves. Required graceful cleanup keeps live mount authority until it succeeds; pending mounts and forced/operator cancellation still abort immediately.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
